summary: Real, dated pain with paid workarounds, but buyers pay for testers (which this refuses to supply), the tester-nudging core is replaceable by a group chat, and the whole market hangs on one Google policy. If anything, test only the rejection-fix/answer-drafter wedge, not the tracker.

demand.evidence: Pain documented (Google Play Help, dev.to, IndieHackers), paid tester services exist (Testers Community $25, Fiverr gigs with unknown prices). No evidence anyone pays for a self-serve own-tester reminder kit; buyers pay for testers.

statusQuo.evidence: Spreadsheet plus WhatsApp nudges, swap groups, free TestPulse SDK or paid testers. Manual cost is low; the costly part is rejection, which the tool cannot prevent since Google judges in-app engagement.

specificity.evidence: Clear segment (solo dev, personal account after 2023-11-13, mid-test or rejected) but no named person; one-use transient cohort.

wedge.evidence: Real wedge is the answer drafter plus rejection-fix list, not the tracker. Shippable in a day with templates.

futureFit.evidence: Market is one Google policy that can change or be automated first-party; cohort shrinks over time.

premises: Developers will pay for a tool rather than chase testers themselves: weakly supported
A self-reported check-in log helps approval: unsupported, Google reviews in-app engagement
The pain persists long enough to build on: policy-dependent
Search and community reach is achievable: plausible but Testers Community already ranks
The kit can stay clear of fake or incentivised testing: yes if it only prompts real people
alternatives: Minimal: rejection-reason to fix-list plus answer-drafter page, no testers or email
Ideal: full tracker, drafter and rejection mode as in the PRD
Lateral: free checklist/guide as lead gen, $19 only for the drafter
Extend an existing repo: reuse the nickelfix rejection-to-fix-list-and-appeal pattern
wedge: Paste Google's rejection reason, get a ranked fix list and draft production-access answers; no tester tracking.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby, Turso/Supabase free, Resend free. Test: onTrack with 15 testers and 3 missing returns 12 with no warning; 4 missing returns 11 with warning. A working M1 does not prove demand.

risks: Self-reported check-ins say nothing about real engagement and invite fake check-ins
Free alternatives cap price and the purchase is one-use
Incentivised-testing policy ambiguity and no approval guarantee
Incumbents already own the search query
killCriteria: Drop if a two-week test with 100+ qualified visitors yields under 5 emails or no one would pay $19, if community threads show buyers want testers supplied rather than a tool, or if Google changes or removes the rule.
